verdict.rationale: Angular's own docs highlight Signals as a first-party, fine-grained reactive state mechanism built into the core framework (angular-docs-1), which serves state-management needs, but the evidence pack contains no mention of a dedicated, separately-versioned first-party state management library (e.g., an official NgRx-equivalent) maintained alongside Angular the way Redux Toolkit or Vuex are for their ecosystems. missing for 10: a named official state-management package/library, its docs/API surface, and independent confirmation it's maintained by the Angular team rather than community (NgRx).
